design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 of trade_in_offers_and_payoffs (category tradein), frozen 2026-09-16 14:05 EDT (Wednesday).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5]}. Assignment: chargeback installment 4, towing deduction 5, title-delay chargeback 5. Value_input floor max(2-1,1) = 1; both edges are value_input.

[Why this is a good test] Desmond asks to square up what his towed-in Altima leaves him owing, spread over installments, with the first payment today. On the opening records he owes nothing (trade equity +20.63): the debt only exists once the agent discovers from the installment rule's two prerequisite sentences that the title-delay chargeback (owed: 53 days after pickup, no title) and the towing fee (owed: Inoperable grade, towed, never booked) must stand on the ledger first, books both with their own 5-factor computations, and then works out today's installment, whose count, basis and shares read the ledger, his purchase history and his finance tier. Getting the number right requires the chargeback clock anchored on the late payoff date, the outlay basis, the staged percentage, two cross-product shares, the round-trip tow and its surcharges, and the late-posting deferral of the towing fee.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: mileage deduction, roll-in, payoff-shortfall payment, lien payoff charge and their four tools. Claimed here (disjoint): tradein_ext_towing_fee_deduction, tradein_ext_title_delay_chargeback, tradein_ext_chargeback_shortfall_installment; tools post_towing_fee_7cb58a13, post_title_delay_chargeback_a143df45, pay_chargeback_shortfall_4672c84f (owner=user). This is the last task; the 7 policies are covered with no overlap. Negative space: the Altima's inspected 143050 vs stated 142600 is within the 1000-mile tolerance, so the mileage policy owes nothing and no mileage deduction is written.

[Problem-tree card] Root tradein_ext_chargeback_shortfall_installment (on_request).
 E1 installment -> title-delay chargeback: value_input, gate shortfall_owed, STATE form: "Today's installment is fixed only after the agreement's ledger carries the title-delay chargeback owed once the title delay chargeback days have passed with no title received date." Only the chargeback policy writes a title-delay chargeback entry. False at opening: title_received_date empty on f2766769-6831-42ad-973a-50ee123e0d1a, pickup 2026-07-25 (period ended 2026-09-08), no chargeback entry, equity +20.63. Resolved by post_title_delay_chargeback_a143df45 (agent). Deleting it: shortfall 199.37 (all towing, deferred), today's installment 0.00, terminal equity +23.84.
 E2 installment -> towing fee: value_input, gate shortfall_owed, STATE form: "Today's installment is not worked out until the agreement's ledger carries the towing fee deduction owed for a vehicle Kestrel collected by tow truck." Only the towing policy writes a towing fee entry. False at opening: variant Inoperable Condition Offer (no hub drop-off: towed), ledger holds quote/credit/payment/payoff only. Deleting it: shortfall 539.16 < 600, one installment, today's amount 446.42.
 Four-point test: both sentences tie this policy's result (today's installment) to a record-visible ledger entry with 'only after' / 'not ... until', name no tool, id or code token, and are scoped to the entry owed (chargeback owed after the period; towing owed for a towed vehicle). One affirmative, one negated, as a collections desk would say them. Derivation: installment rule -> ledger lacks both entries -> chargeback rule (period passed, no title) and towing rule (Inoperable, towed) are the writers -> book both -> compute. Order: towing and chargeback are parallel and commute (swap replay identical); the installment is last. user_scenario names neither; tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Towing and chargeback (subject tradein_value_deducted): tradein_pickup_inspection.value_on_picked_up, status picked_up, satisfied. tradein_title_receipt.chargeback_timing is retired as a general deduction gate by the mileage policy's declared overwrite; the chargeback policy restates it verbatim in its own rule ('A title-delay chargeback may be taken only after the title delay chargeback days counted from the pickup date have passed with no title received date.') with the base counting sentence: pickup 2026-07-25 = day 0, Inoperable 45 days, last day 2026-09-08, allowed from 2026-09-09; on 2026-09-08 it would not be allowed, on 2026-09-16 it is. Installment (subject tradein_negative_equity_settled): tradein_negative_equity.shortfall_state, picked_up, satisfied; the chargeback payment days (10) run from the 2026-09-16 chargeback to 2026-09-26, the window in which the remaining 535.95 is due.

[Business-object card] Target: agreement f2766769-6831-42ad-973a-50ee123e0d1a (2013 Nissan Altima 2.5 S, VIN 1N4AL3AP5DN257318) linked to the Tucson order 1c14dc62-e3d3-4a5a-8ce0-c7113e4c1e61. Ledger: quote 41beeeaf-fdd2-4866-8d5f-ba11985a3424 (2604.37, ref 274418), credit b146f1e6-d325-443f-97f4-2571a7a54798 (1850.00), his covering payment 4b975428-17b2-435a-a9db-1100218da800 (775.00, 2026-07-27), payoff 8a5d1cf4-1408-490c-9d6a-52e570935818 (2604.37, 2026-07-29). Cross records: delivery f922f8a0-4d6b-4d18-ae9f-958eb18be264 (Local Home Delivery, 95 mi, completed 2026-07-21), finance 7b3a767b-7a74-417e-ab06-43ca900c9270 (Tier B, active, autopay, ledger 98a50e25-cf27-460b-a8a6-73ffc653ec1a/0443a7f5-ee8c-44b1-80e8-d5ab20d503bf/fa48413f-a5be-4cfa-b55d-3988a8fe0ef6), title order cdf6500b-ad65-4e3f-99dc-80de3626fbda (kestrel_auto_finance, registered), KestrelCare Powertrain Plus eba485a4-96a8-4357-8ac6-5ca2706792d9 with its limit 83c50620-4503-4916-93c6-6bd1885b021b, purchase charges 18911fca-d886-4bdd-8b5d-fa6b3e12129f and f2d9320e-bc57-4552-8b27-78c44d2e87f0 (two Kestrel purchases; the 2023 Kia Soul order 6918fce6-9b0a-4ae9-840b-274fac451a52 and its payment e543d94f-59b1-42bd-8682-f26bf40a7bfe; the Tucson down payment ae35fbda-f345-4856-9b82-453f9b107c9f and finance proceeds d2236dca-66a9-42a9-9236-8a8094263d77). Near-misses: the two purchase payments are not vehicle-price charges; the 2023 order is not the linked purchase (its delivery/finance/title do not exist); the customer payment entry dated 2026-07-27 is before the payoff, so the clock anchors on the late payoff, not on it.

[Factor cards (solve.py 1, handling-time world)]
 Towing 220.00 (baseline 289.00): tow_trip_pattern M (towed 4 days after delivery -> a trip of its own, priced as the greater of the 149.00 towing fee and the round-trip mileage charge 1.50 x (190 - 40) = 225.00; baseline fee plus one-way mileage gives 225.20); tow_included_by_method P (Local Home Delivery 40; baseline 238.00); tow_weekend_hook P (Saturday 50.00; baseline 180.00); tow_distance_rate P (95 mi -> 1.50; baseline 280.00); tow_carry_share P, multi-source, cross-difficulty finance (active Kestrel finance + KestrelCare on the Tucson -> 0.8; baseline 275.00).
 Chargeback 559.79 (baseline 1850.00): chargeback_clock_anchor M (payoff 4 days after pickup > 3 -> clock from 2026-07-29, 49 days; baseline 979.63 at 53 days/70); staged_percentage P (<= 52 days -> 40; baseline 1399.47); lien_outlay_basis M (payoff less his payment 1829.37; baseline 566.10); title_collateral P, cross-difficulty title (registered Kestrel lien -> 0.9; baseline 621.99); finance_standing P, multi-source, cross-difficulty finance (autopay + 2 autopay installments in 12 months -> 0.85; baseline 658.57).
 Installment 223.21 (baseline 759.16): installment_count_by_size P (759.16 in [600, 1200) -> 2; baseline 446.42); towing_installment_placement M (towing posted 53 days after pickup > 30 -> the towing fee rides with the last installment, today's figure (759.16 - 220.00) / 2 = 269.58; baseline even spread 379.58 gives 314.29); repeat_buyer P, cross-difficulty purchase (2 vehicle-price charges -> 0.9; baseline 248.01); finance_tier_installment P, cross-difficulty finance (Tier B 660 -> 0.92; baseline 242.62).
 Every factor moves its result; each all-baseline figure differs from gold; history and cross-category floors hold (check_compute --task 1 OK).

[Overrides declared] towing: base 'and the towing fee when the vehicle is towed.' replaced by the distance-priced towing sentence; chargeback: base 'The chargeback is the grade's chargeback percentage of the value credited, deducted as a title_delay_chargeback entry;' replaced by the basis x percentage x shares sentence; installment: the two base sentences that make the whole shortfall due within the chargeback payment days, replaced by the installment sentence (rest still due within those days).

[Seed rows and why they exist] Every row is read by a gold read and moves a figure: agreement and its four ledger rows (equity, clock, basis, posting lag); delivery (distance, trip day, method); finance contract and ledger (status, autopay track, tier); title order (collateral); service contract and its limit (KestrelCare on the purchase, contract in force); purchase orders and their charges/payments (linked order; repeat-buyer count). Nothing ignites another obligation: the Tucson order is completed with balance 0, its finance contract is current (next due 2026-10-15), its title is registered.

[Persona design] Desmond is brief and practical; volunteers only the goal (square up what the trade-in leaves him owing, spread, first payment today) and his mobile number; credentials and the old loan account only when asked; reacts to a tow or a title explanation only after the agent raises it; pays exactly the quoted amount with the quoted reference through the handed-over tool; closes once told the payment is recorded and what remains by when. He never mentions a fee, a chargeback or a computation.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB, SSN4) -> agreements -> trade ledger -> purchase orders -> purchase ledger -> delivery -> finance contract -> finance ledger -> title order -> service contracts -> service contract history -> unlock+call towing 220.00 -> unlock+call chargeback 559.79 -> unlock user tool, customer pays 223.21. Terminal equity -535.95, due by 2026-09-26.

[Verification] solve.py 1 (results above), edges.py 1 (skip chargeback -> 0.00 / +23.84; skip towing -> 446.42; swap identical terminal; gold terminal -535.95); per-task gates check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding / check_cross_fire --task 1 all OK. Draft recomputation from visible context: the KB prose of the three policies, the tool schemas, the persona and the lookups yield the same three writes, order and amounts; the only id passed is the agreement reference from the lookup.

[Revision log] (1) check_extended: the staged-percentage factor's only binding read no record -> the clock was split into a start-date binding (anchor method) and a day count owned by the percentage factor. (2) edges.py: with the whole towing fee deferred, skipping the towing write left today's installment unchanged (edge not load-bearing) -> installment lines moved to 600/1200 so the towing fee carries the shortfall into two installments. (3) check_compute: the finance standing ladder counted late fees, which the world (correctly) has none of, so no cross-difficulty evidence row was read -> the ladder now counts installments posted by autopay in the last twelve months (two seeded rows), rule/compute/basis/ladder/trace updated.

[Round 2 rework - audit audits/policy_task/trade_in_offers_and_payoffs]
 F-2 / F-T1-1 (towing had no honest method factor): tow_trip_pattern now selects the pricing form, not a mile multiplier - a tow on its own trip is billed at the greater of the grade's towing fee and the round-trip mileage charge (minimum-or-mileage), a tow riding with the delivery run is the towing fee alone, otherwise fee plus one-way mileage (rule, compute binding towing_charge, basis, ladder, baseline). To keep every factor load-bearing under the max() form the delivery distance was set to 95 miles (inside the Local Home Delivery 100-mile radius): towing 220.00 (was 218.00); the shortfall becomes 759.16, today's installment stays 223.21, terminal equity -535.95.
 F-3 / F-T1-2 (installment had no honest method factor): late_towing_deferral replaced by towing_installment_placement, which decides which installment carries the towing fee - the last one (late-posted), today's (posted within the recent-posting days) or none in particular (even spread, the baseline); today's figure is computed by a different allocation rule per tier.
 O-2: the towing policy now declares its own overwrite of the title-delay timing sentence with the rule sentence 'The waiting period after pickup that holds back a title-delay chargeback does not hold back a towing deduction.'
 O-5: the chargeback's autopay count is restricted to the linked purchase's finance contract (finance_contract_id filter); figures unchanged (one contract).
 Re-run: solve.py 1 -> 220.00 / 559.79 / 223.21; skip chargeback -> 0.00, terminal +23.84; skip towing -> 446.42; swap identical; full gate block OK.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Fairweather, a forty-six-year-old IT support technician in Raleigh, North Carolina, calling Kestrel Auto customer care on a Wednesday afternoon from your desk. You talk in short, practical sentences and you want this off your plate. In July you traded your old 2013 Nissan Altima 2.5 S, which would not start any more, toward the 2022 Hyundai Tucson SEL you bought from Kestrel, and Kestrel towed the Altima away. Since late August Kestrel has kept emailing you for a lien release letter from Piedmont Ridge Federal Credit Union, your old lender on the Altima, and the credit union keeps telling you it will look into it. You open with: "I keep getting emails about a lien release letter for the Altima I traded in, and I just can't get one out of my old credit union. I'd like to square up whatever that trade-in leaves me owing, but I can't do a lump sum, so I want to spread it and make the first payment today." You are fine with the representative doing whatever Kestrel needs to do on its side to work out what you owe, and the payment itself you want to make yourself, today.

You give your mobile number, 9195552604, right away so they can find you. When asked to verify, you give your date of birth, 1979-11-08, and the last four of your Social Security number, 2159; if they need one more detail you can add your email, dfairweather.nc@gmail.com, or your ZIP code, 27606. Only if they ask about the old loan do you say it was with Piedmont Ridge Federal Credit Union, account number 275519. You do not know any amounts or reference numbers on the trade-in and you tell them to go by Kestrel's records.

You never bring up fees, charges or how Kestrel works things out. When the representative says something has to be booked on the trade-in first, you say okay, go ahead. If they mention a towing charge, you say that's right, it had to be towed because it wouldn't start. If they explain what the missing title means for your trade-in, you say you understand and to go ahead. When they set up the payment for you and give you the trade-in agreement reference and the amount for today, you pay exactly that amount with exactly that reference from your checking account, and you read back the confirmation if they ask. You do not suggest an amount of your own and you do not ask for a discount. Once the representative tells you today's payment is recorded and what is left to pay and by when, you say thanks, you'll handle the rest before then, and you end the call without asking about anything else.

Per-mile rate: the 95-mile one-way distance is longer than the 50-mile long-tow line, 1.50 (baseline 2.00). Towing charge: the Tucson delivery completed 2026-07-21 and the Altima was towed 2026-07-25, a different day, so the tow was a trip of its own and the charge is the greater of the 149.00 towing fee and 1.50 x (2 x 95 - 40) = 225.00, that is 225.00 (baseline: 149.00 + 1.50 x (95 - 40) = 231.50). Hook surcharge: 2026-07-25 was a Saturday, 50.00 (baseline none). Tow share: active Kestrel Auto Finance contract and a KestrelCare contract on the Tucson, 0.8. (225.00 + 50.00) x 0.8 = 220.00.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.chargeback_amount: Value 559.79. Allowed: pickup 2026-07-25 is day 0, the 45-day period ends 2026-09-08, a chargeback is allowed from 2026-09-09; on 2026-09-16 no title received date stands. Clock: the lien payoff entry is dated 2026-07-29, 4 days after pickup, more than the 3 prompt-payoff days, so the clock runs from 2026-07-29: 49 days (baseline from pickup: 53). Percentage: 49 is no more than the 52 early-stage days, 40 percent (baseline grade percentage 100). Basis: a payoff entry (2604.37) and a customer payment entry (775.00) stand, so 2604.37 - 775.00 = 1829.37 (baseline value credited 1850.00).
